misconceptions.description: Writing a learning goal that has no measurable outcome or deadline, so progress cannot be checked
misconceptions.trigger: plan says 'get better at coding' or 'learn more about data'
misconceptions.feedback: Make goals measurable and dated. 'Build and publish a 3-page portfolio site by August 1' can be checked; 'get better at coding' cannot.

misconceptions.description: Listing milestones with no artifact or proof that would show the milestone was reached
misconceptions.trigger: milestone is 'understand Excel' with no deliverable attached
misconceptions.feedback: Attach a proof to each milestone, such as a finished pivot-table file or a live page URL, so a future reviewer or you can confirm it happened.

misconceptions.description: Planning to learn many large skills simultaneously with no sequence or prerequisite order
misconceptions.trigger: plan lists ten advanced topics for one month with no ordering
misconceptions.feedback: Sequence by prerequisite and pick a realistic next step. Master spreadsheet formulas before databases; one solid, sequenced goal beats ten unordered ones.
